dedupe_keys.name: comparative case study of the rhine erft july 2021 and emilia romagna may 2023 floods directed

description: This report from the EU Horizon Europe project DIRECTED compares two of Europe's most damaging recent floods, in the Rhine-Erft district of Germany in July 2021 and in Emilia-Romagna, Italy, in May 2023, to draw lessons on preparedness, emergency management, recovery and resilience. It draws on open data, academic research and the project's Real World Labs in both regions. Emilia-Romagna received six months of rain in 36 hours, and Rhine-Erft more than 200 mm in one day; the Italian floods caused 17 deaths, displaced over 36,000 people and caused damage of about 8.8 to 9 billion euro, while the German floods caused 189 deaths nationally, 11 in Rhine-Erft. It contrasts Italy's centralised civil protection and early warnings with the German response. Version 6 (30 September 2025) is by Irvine, Mazzoli, Pancioli, Löhrlein and others, and is available free on Zenodo as a PDF under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: it is a narrative synthesis. It informs emergency response and recovery planning for flood-hit infrastructure; a related record is the Global Flood Database.
